title: Single key remap not working
author: Manlibear

status.label: ShareMouse marker collision identified
status.detail: The supplied trace shows ShareMouse using dwExtraInfo=5. Current main treats any event with bit 0 set as Keyboard Manager input and skips it, which also matches 5.

next_action: Approve a design to distinguish Keyboard Manager's own injected events from external input, then verify the reported 1-to-2 remap through ShareMouse on a current build.

judgment.rationale: The reporter's diagnostic trace and a maintainer's analysis identify a concrete input-filter collision: ShareMouse sets KBDLLHOOKSTRUCT::dwExtraInfo to 5, while current main classifies an event as Keyboard Manager-generated whenever bit 0 is set. Since 5 & 1 is nonzero, ShareMouse input is skipped by the single-key remapper. A current-version reproduction is still useful, but the source predicate and existing trace support a focused design.
evidence: The original issue reports that a 1-to-2 remap still prints 1 when the input comes from a MacBook Pro through ShareMouse; a directly connected Windows keyboard remaps correctly.
The attached 2021 diagnostic trace repeatedly records incoming key events with dwExtraInfo=5, and a maintainer states that this causes Keyboard Manager to ignore them.
At upstream main 0b1dd814878f0dfbb07787d9c3e52a2897b6f769, KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp:34-37 tests dwExtraInfo with KEYBOARDMANAGER_INJECTED_FLAG.
At the same revision, shared_constants.h:7-8 defines KEYBOARDMANAGER_INJECTED_FLAG as 0x1, so an external marker value of 5 satisfies the current filter.
A 2026 maintainer comment asks whether the issue persists on v0.100.2 or newer; that confirmation from the original reporter is unanswered.
judgment.recommended_action: Design a collision-resistant way to recognize Keyboard Manager's own injected events, preserve non-transitive remapping, and verify it against the existing ShareMouse 1-to-2 reproduction.

fix_assessment.rationale: The reported external marker and the current low-bit predicate directly match, but the issue's last direct reproduction predates current PowerToys and the reporter has not confirmed v0.100.2 or newer.

proposed_fixes.title: Avoid treating ShareMouse input as Keyboard Manager injection
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Keyboard Manager suppresses input when any bit in dwExtraInfo overlaps KEYBOARDMANAGER_INJECTED_FLAG (0x1). ShareMouse uses dwExtraInfo=5, so its physical key event is mistaken for Keyboard Manager's own injected event and never reaches the single-key remap path.
plan: Trace all Keyboard Manager input-injection sites and the GeneratedByKBM predicate to define one consistent provenance contract.

Replace the collision-prone low-bit test with either an exact, collision-resistant Keyboard Manager marker or explicit tracking of the events Keyboard Manager injected; do not suppress arbitrary external dwExtraInfo values merely because their lowest bit is set.
Add regression coverage showing that an external event with dwExtraInfo=5 is remapped while Keyboard Manager's own generated events remain non-transitive.
verification: With ShareMouse supplying the reported 1-to-2 key mapping, pressing 1 produces 2 on a current PowerToys build.
A directly attached Windows keyboard continues to produce 2 for the same mapping.
Keyboard Manager-generated events are still excluded from recursive remapping, including events carrying its new provenance marker.

confidence.rationale: The existing trace gives the external marker value and current source uses the exact conflicting low-bit test; a current-build reproduction and injection-path regression tests are still needed.

issue_context.summary: Single-key remaps are bypassed for keyboard input forwarded from a Mac through ShareMouse, while the same remap works with a keyboard connected directly to Windows.
known_information: The issue originally used PowerToys 0.43.0 as administrator on Windows 10, with a MacBook Pro running macOS 11.5.2 connected through ShareMouse.
The reported simple reproduction is a 1-to-2 remap; input forwarded through ShareMouse still prints 1, while a directly attached Windows keyboard prints 2.
The supplied trace records ShareMouse keyboard events with KBDLLHOOKSTRUCT::dwExtraInfo=5, and a maintainer identified the low-bit marker collision.
A 2023 commenter confirmed a similar issue on v0.69.1; another commenter described it on v0.78.0.
A maintainer asked in July 2026 whether the original report persists on v0.100.2 or newer; the original reporter has not answered.
Current main defines the Keyboard Manager injected flag as 0x1 and tests it with a bitwise AND.
inferences: The current marker predicate still appears capable of suppressing ShareMouse events whose dwExtraInfo is 5.
A current-version reproduction would establish whether ShareMouse still emits the same marker and whether the same event-filter path remains active.
issue_context.analysis: The old diagnostic evidence and the current source predicate form a direct explanation for the reported behavior: the event metadata from ShareMouse collides with Keyboard Manager's low-bit marker, causing the remapper to skip input. The fix must continue to prevent Keyboard Manager's own synthetic events from being remapped recursively, so the marker/tracking approach should be selected with all injection call sites in view. Reproduce the simple 1-to-2 case on a current build before implementation.
initial_investigation: Read the live issue body and all 20 comments, including the original diagnostic trace, the wired-keyboard control result, later confirmations, and the unanswered current-version question.
Inspected upstream main at 0b1dd814878f0dfbb07787d9c3e52a2897b6f769: KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp:34-37 and src/common/interop/shared_constants.h:7-8.
Checked direct PR references; no covering PR or linked duplicate was found.

information_gaps.information: Whether ShareMouse still supplies the same dwExtraInfo marker and the 1-to-2 remap still fails on a current PowerToys build.
information_gaps.why_needed: The available diagnostic trace is from 2021, while current main still contains a matching low-bit filter; a current run will verify the remaining behavior before implementation.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Repeat the same ShareMouse 1-to-2 mapping on a current stable build and compare it with a directly connected Windows keyboard.

actions.label: Approve injected-event marker design
actions.note: Preserve non-transitive remapping while distinguishing Keyboard Manager-generated events from external input metadata.

actions.label: Reproduce ShareMouse single-key remap
actions.note: The issue includes an old diagnostic trace and exact mapping; confirm the same behavior on a current build without requesting another archive.

reproduce.title: Test a single-key remap with ShareMouse input
reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys 0.100.2 or newer; record the exact build
prerequisites: Windows 10 or Windows 11 with Keyboard Manager enabled
A Mac keyboard forwarded to the Windows machine through ShareMouse
A directly attached Windows keyboard for the control test
setup: Configure the reported single-key remap 1 to 2.
steps: Press 1 using the Mac keyboard forwarded through ShareMouse.
Repeat by pressing 1 on a keyboard connected directly to Windows.
Record the PowerToys version and compare the resulting characters.
reproduce.expected_result: Both input sources produce 2, and Keyboard Manager's own synthetic events are not recursively remapped.
reproduce.setup_prompt: On a Windows test machine with Keyboard Manager enabled, connect a Mac keyboard through ShareMouse, configure 1-to-2, and compare the forwarded key with a directly attached Windows keyboard.
